name: T-Hybrid Generation
tagline: T-Hybrid: 541 PS, an eTurbo and 400 volts
description:
The 992.2 is the first 911 generation to carry a high-voltage electrical system, and Porsche's engineers arrived at the shortest possible route to it. Unveiled on 28 May 2024 alongside the revived Carrera, the debut model was the Carrera GTS with the T-Hybrid system: a 3.6-litre boxer with a single electrically assisted exhaust-gas turbocharger, a permanent-magnet synchronous motor buried inside the eight-speed PDK, and a 1.9 kWh, 400-volt battery no bigger than a conventional starter battery. The motor spins the turbo to speed before the exhaust gas arrives, so boost is instant — full system torque of 610 Nm is on tap below 2,000 rpm. Unlike a plug-in hybrid, the battery is never drained for propulsion; it is there to recover energy and to fill gaps. Porsche cites a weight penalty of just 50 kg over the outgoing GTS, against roughly eight times that for a typical PHEV.

The Carrera line was re-cut around the new powertrain. The base 992.2 Carrera keeps a 2,981 cc twin-turbo six — now with the old GTS turbochargers and Turbo-type intercooling for 394 PS — while the long-absent Carrera S returned in January 2025 with 480 PS, closing the gap to the old 992.1 GTS. All-wheel drive came back in July 2025 with the 473 hp Carrera 4S Coupé and Cabriolet and the Targa 4S, bringing the AWD count to six. There is deliberately no base Carrera 4: Porsche states the standard Carrera is not offered with all-wheel drive. The Turbo S followed at IAA Munich in September 2025, taking the T-Hybrid to its extreme with two eTurbos, 711 PS, 322 km/h and a 7:03.92 Nürburgring Nordschleife lap — about 14 seconds quicker than the 992.1 car despite carrying 85 kg more.

Running the other way from the hybrids, the GT3 doubled down on what it always was. The 2025 GT3 and GT3 Touring retained the 4.0-litre naturally aspirated six at 510 PS and a 9,000 rpm redline, survived Euro 7 with two particulate filters and four catalytic converters at the cost of 20 Nm, and compensated with a final drive 8 per cent shorter than before. The Weissach Package became available on a non-RS GT3 for the first time. On 14 April 2026 the GT3 S/C arrived — the first open-top GT3 in history, manual-only, two-seater, and the lightest open-top 911 in the range. For the manual faithful, the Carrera T arrived as the only three-pedal 911 below the GT3, and in August 2026 Porsche restored a manual Carrera S to North America as an MT Package exclusive.

One open question remains at the close of 2026: no 992.2 GT3 RS has been announced. Prototypes have been photographed at the Nürburgring since mid-2025, and spy photographers read the exhaust note as turbocharged, but Porsche has published nothing. The roster entry is retained and marked unconfirmed rather than guessed. Alongside the range, Porsche's collector arm has been busy — the Spirit 70 (1,500), the GT3 90 F. A. Porsche (90) and the ten individually configured Carrera 4 GTS Tribute to Transfăgărășan cars.

variants.description: The 992.2 Carrera was the entry point to the T-Hybrid era, unveiled on 28 May 2024 in Coupé and Cabriolet form. Its 2,981 cc twin-turbo flat-six keeps the previous GTS turbochargers and adopts the charge-air cooler from the outgoing Turbo, lifting output to 290 kW (394 PS; 388 hp) and 450 Nm while cutting emissions. Performance is 4.1 s to 100 km/h — 3.9 s with the Sport Chrono Package — and 294 km/h (183 mph). The Cabriolet gives up 2 km/h and 0.2 s. Porsche lists no manual and no all-wheel-drive Carrera 4 in this generation; the T is the manual-only route and the 4S covers the AWD entry point. Figures are Coupé DIN unless stated.

variants.description: With the Carrera S gone PDK-only, the T became the only three-pedal 911 below the GT3 — and for the first time the manual-only model is also offered as a Cabriolet. It uses the base Carrera's 2,981 cc twin-turbo six (394 PS / 388 hp, 450 Nm) but sheds weight: 1,490 kg DIN in Coupé form makes it the lightest 992.2, 30 kg below the Carrera. Rear-axle steering, PASM dampers tuned specifically for the T and an open-pore laminated-walnut gear knob come as standard, and 70 per cent of 992.1 T buyers already chose the manual. At 4.5 s to 100 km/h it is the slowest 992.2 Coupé, which is rather the point.

variants.description: Porsche re-created the Carrera S in January 2025 to slot between the Carrera and the hybrid GTS, delivering the performance of the outgoing 992.1 GTS without the 3.6-litre engine. The 2,981 cc twin-turbo six gained 30 hp to 353 kW (480 PS; 473 hp) and 530 Nm thanks to new turbochargers and intercooling carried over from the 911 Turbo. Coupé and Cabriolet are offered, both with the eight-speed PDK only — the manual version returned to North America a year and a half later as the separate MT Package car. With Sport Chrono the Coupé reaches 100 km/h in 3.3 s and 308 km/h (191 mph).

variants.description: Announced on 2 July 2025 for the 2026 model year, the Carrera 4S brought all-wheel drive back to the 992.2 after an absence of four years. It adopts the upgraded Carrera S engine — 473 hp (353 kW) and 390 lb-ft, up 30 hp — with charge-air cooling taken from the 911 Turbo, and an eight-speed PDK sending power to all four wheels. Standard equipment expanded sharply: 408 mm front and 380 mm rear brakes from the previous GTS, Sport Exhaust, revised dampers, PTV Plus and staggered 20/21-inch Carrera S wheels. Rear-axle steering is optional on the 4S Coupé and Cabriolet; with the trio the 911 now has six all-wheel-drive variants.

It carries the same upgraded 3.0-litre twin-turbo six and eight-speed PDK as the 4S, with the same enlarged GTS brakes, silver Sport Exhaust tailpipes and reworked dampers. variants.description: The first road-legal 911 with a performance hybrid, revealed on 28 May 2024 and in production from June. A single wastegate-free eTurbo replaces the old twin-turbo arrangement: its motor sits between compressor and turbine, spinning the shaft instantly and doubling as an 11 kW generator. The 3.6-litre boxer (bore grew 6 mm, stroke 4.6 mm) is 110 mm shallower because the belt drive is gone, freeing space for the inverter and DC-DC converter. The PDK motor adds up to 150 Nm and 40 kW from idle. Nürburgring time: 7:16.93, some 8.7 s quicker than the 992.1 GTS despite 47 kg more mass. Only 50 kg of the hybrid is real penalty.

variants.description: The heaviest and rarest shape in the 992.2 GTS family: a Targa that carries the full T-Hybrid system, 541 PS and 610 Nm, and still runs to 312 km/h. Porsche quotes 3.1 s to 100 km/h and 1,745 kg DIN — 100 kg more than the Carrera GTS Coupé and the same as the Carrera 4 GTS Cabriolet, thanks to the Targa bar, the magnesium roof structure and the wraparound rear glass. Rear-axle steering and PASM come as standard with this body style, and the front luggage compartment shrinks to 135 litres with 163 litres behind the seats.

variants.description: Revealed on 18 October 2024 as a 25th-anniversary double premiere, the 992.2 GT3 launched simultaneously with a fixed rear wing and as a wingless Touring Package car. Porsche consulted some 2,000 GT3 owners before developing it, and the brief was clear: no turbos, no batteries, no drive modes. Meeting Euro 7 while keeping the naturally aspirated flat-six cost 20 Nm — down from 470 to 450 Nm — with revised cylinder heads, camshafts from the GT3 RS, flow-optimised throttle bodies and better oil coolers doing the work. Power and the 9,000 rpm redline are unchanged. The Weissach Package, previously reserved for the RS, is available for the first time on a standard GT3, and the Clubsport package is offered at no cost.

variants.description: For the first time the GT3 Touring Package was available from launch rather than as a later arrival, and the designation traces back to the 1973 Carrera RS 2.7. Dropping the fixed swan-neck wing for an extendable spoiler with a Gurney flap and revised underbody fins restores the classic 911 roofline — the drop in drag is why the manual Touring, at 313 km/h, outruns the winged PDK car at 311 km/h. The Lightweight Package adds a body-coloured CFRP roof, CFRP anti-roll bar, coupling rods and rear shear panel, forged magnesium wheels, lightweight door panels and the shortened S/T gear lever. All GT3 mechanicals are shared, including the 9,000 rpm flat-six.

variants.name: 911 GT3 RS
variants.description: PLACEHOLDER — NO SUCH CAR HAS BEEN ANNOUNCED. No 992.2 911 GT3 RS exists as an announced production model as of 1 October 2026; only camouflaged prototypes have been reported. The roster entry is retained (roster ids are stable) but every specification field is null, so the specification plate renders a dash plus the note that explains it and the site cannot present this car with real numbers. What is on record: prototypes of a 992.2-phase GT3 RS have been photographed testing at the Nürburgring since mid-2025, most recently in September 2026, with a revised front bumper, canards, a wider diffuser and a three-element active rear wing retaining DRS. Spy photography and soundtrack recordings have led outlets to conclude forced induction is likely, with power estimates from 650 hp upward, but Porsche has only ever said that a turbocharged or electrified future GT3 is possible. Reveal dates reported for August 2026 did not materialise, and the current on-sale car remains the 992.1 GT3 RS (386 kW / 525 PS / 518 hp at 8,500 rpm) — that figure belongs to the 992.1 and is deliberately not repeated in this record. If and when Porsche announces the car, this entry becomes a normal variant; until then it is a hole in the lineup, not a car.

variants.name: 911 GT3 S/C
variants.engine: 3,996 cc (4.0 L) naturally aspirated flat-six, 102.0 × 81.5 mm, 9,000 rpm redline; two particulate filters and four catalytic converters

variants.description: Unveiled on 14 April 2026 as a 2027 model, the GT3 S/C is the first 911 GT3 Cabriolet in the badge's 27-year history. The fabric roof is fully automatic, opens and closes in about 12 seconds up to 60 km/h, and uses magnesium panels in the roof structure so the silhouette stays coupe-like; an electric wind deflector deploys in two seconds. Weight is held to 1,497 kg with S/T-derived CFRP doors and fenders, a CFRP boot lid, rear anti-roll bar and shear panel, forged magnesium centre-lock wheels and standard PCCB. Unlike the 2019 Speedster, it is explicitly not a limited edition, and it is the first open-top 911 with a double-wishbone front axle.

It is a 992.2 Carrera GTS Cabriolet dressed in Olive Neo with Bronzite Sport Classic wheels, black soft top and windscreen frame, three bonnet stripes carrying elongated 911 lettering, and a '70' door roundel that can be deleted at the customer's request. variants.description: Appended variant. Announced on 13 August 2026 and debuting at Monterey Car Week, the MT Package brings a six-speed manual Carrera S back to North America for the first time since 2019 — the 992.2 had launched PDK-only. North America is the sole market, and the package adds a higher specification than the PDK Carrera S while minimising weight: Sport Chrono, rear-axle steering, GT Sport steering wheel and larger brakes are standard, and carbon-fibre bucket seats and PCCB are optional — the last of which is not available on the Carrera T. Curb weight is 3,327 lb in Coupé form. US pricing starts at $167,100 for the Coupé and $181,000 for the Cabriolet.

variants.description: Appended variant. Ten individually configured 992.2 Carrera 4 GTS Coupés built through the Porsche Sonderwunsch programme to celebrate 50 years of the Transfăgărășan, the 90-kilometre Romanian mountain road that also marked the 911 Turbo's 50th in 2024. Each car carries 'Tribute to Transfăgărășan' door decals, a special B-pillar badge, engine-grille slats in the Romanian blue-yellow-red, illuminated door sill guards, embroidered headrests and an embossed centre armrest. The hero car, in Paint to Sample Graphite Grey with Guards Red wheel spokes and headlight rings, was delivered in August 2025 and driven straight onto the road it honours. No mechanical changes were made.
variants.production: 10 cars, each individually specified by its owner with the Sonderwunsch and Style Porsche teams (first delivered August 2025)
